text:
raj: FYI I'm starting Axon-7B onboarding (community Gemma fork). Int4 conversion finished; runs but quality on long contexts tanks. Suspect rotary/indexmap or tokenizer offsets. Anyone seen weird token-id drift when converting Gemma->Qwen style tokenmaps? :thinking:

emma: Can you paste a minimal reproduce and sample outputs? Also what quant toolchain (our int4 pipeline or bitsandbytes?)

raj: Using our int4 pipeline (quantize_v2). Short prompt Q/A looks fine; with ~1k context the model repeats and drops answers. Example outputs attached in the experiment run (S3 link): s3://redwood-expts/axon7b/2026-03-19/run-42/outputs.txt

kevin: Two quick suspects: 1) tokenizer mapping adds a sentinel/pad offset so rotary positions shift relative to KV cache; 2) rotary scale/base mismatch — some Gemma variants baked headwise scaling. Did you preserve original rope base when converting?

maria: I saw similar earlier — when token ids are remapped off-by-one the kvcache indices align to wrong tokens and attention attends to shifted positions. Logs look like repeated ngram patterns.

sasha: Bench numbers I ran earlier on a different fork:
- LM eval ppl (wiki) short (<=128): 8.1 (baseline 7.9)
- LM eval ppl long (<=2048): 19.6 (baseline 12.4)
- Generation BLEU/ROUGE drop visible in >512 tokens
So it's not pure quant noise, seems positional/rotary loss.

raj: here's the converter snippet I used:
```
# tokenmap conversion pseudo
for i, tok in enumerate(old_vocab):
  new_id = byte_align(tok)  # naive mapping
  out_map[i] = new_id
```
No special handling for pad/unk.

kevin: There's the issue. Some Gemma->Qwen conversions require inserting a reserved token at id 0 (pad) and shifting the rest. Also Gemma rotary implementation uses headwise scaling factor 1.03 in checkpoints we saw. Try: 1) apply explicit token-id remap table preserving special ids, 2) swap rotary scale to 1.0 vs original and evaluate.

ci-bot: [artifact uploaded] Axon7B int4 run-42 logs at s3://redwood-expts/axon7b/2026-03-19/run-42/logs.tar.gz

emma: Can you run a quick smoke that compares identical input with two prefixes that only differ in tokenization (one using remap table)? We need a minimal test that isolates kvcache indexing from quantization error.

raj: Running that now. Quick diff: with naive mapping top tokens are: "the time is now" -> model outputs looping 'now now now' after 600 tokens. With explicit remap (preserve pad/unk) output remains coherent to ~1600 tokens. So seems confirm remap helps.

maria: Nice. What about rotary base/scale? Any change if you set rope_alpha/scale param to original Gemma values?

raj: I toggled rotary_scale between 1.0 and 1.03 in the runtime. 1.03 gets slightly better on short contexts but long-context still worse than remapped run. So primary win is token remap+kvcache alignment.

kevin: Sounds like two orthogonal fixes: token remap to align ids and then tune rotary scale/headwise params to recover small perf delta. For int4, also check quant clipping config — asymmetric clipping can amplify aliasing. Try symmetric zero-point clipping and re-run.

sasha: Adding numbers after raj's remap (run-43):
- PPL short: 8.0
- PPL long: 13.1 (huge improvement)
- Generation coherency at 2k tokens: restored (no looping)

emma: Great. Can someone create a tiny repro script and a unit test that asserts kvcache alignment for remapped vs naive mapping? We should add to model-conversion tests.

raj: I'll draft a repro and push a branch. Plan: 1) add remap table generation that preserves special tokens; 2) add unit test that feeds a synthetic token sequence designed to catch off-by-one index shifts; 3) run full int4 quant with symmetric clipping. I'll ping infra to run through dedicated cluster.

maria: Also add an eval A/B against our standard long-context eval set (ACCEPTANCE_LONG). If run-43 passes, we can promote Axon-7B to staging and roll to dedicated pool for more load testing.

kevin: One more note — check export of rotary params from original checkpoint. Some exporters pack per-head scale in metadata; if converter drops that metadata runtime will default to 1.0. We should preserve per-head attributes.

ci-bot: [pipeline note] queued int4 quant job: expt/axon7b/remap+symclip/run-44 (queued on dedicated gpu pool). ETA ~45m.

raj: Thanks all. Will send the repro branch link when ready. If run-44 looks good I think this is safe to promote. :thumbsup:

emma: Awesome work — thanks for triaging quickly. +1 to tests in conversion pipeline. :eyes:
